runs.name: find
runs.command: thinkthen find 'Which line gives the refund deadline?' < policy.txt
runs.input:
Returns need the original receipt.
Refunds are issued within 30 days of purchase.
Shipping is free on orders over $50.
Gift cards cannot be exchanged for cash.
runs.output: Refunds are issued within 30 days of purchase.
runs.see: find prints the line with the 30 day refund deadline.

runs.name: find-answer
runs.command: thinkthen find --details 'Which line gives the refund deadline?' < policy.txt | jq -r '.answer.probabilities|tojson'
runs.input:
Returns need the original receipt.
Refunds are issued within 30 days of purchase.
Shipping is free on orders over $50.
Gift cards cannot be exchanged for cash.
runs.see: The second line holds all of the weight.

runs.name: find-none
runs.command: thinkthen find --none 'Which line says how to cancel an order?' < policy.txt
runs.input:
Returns need the original receipt.
Refunds are issued within 30 days of purchase.
Shipping is free on orders over $50.
Gift cards cannot be exchanged for cash.
runs.see: No line says how to cancel, so find prints nothing and exits 3.

runs.name: find-forced
runs.command: thinkthen find 'Which line says how to cancel an order?' < policy.txt
runs.input:
Returns need the original receipt.
Refunds are issued within 30 days of purchase.
Shipping is free on orders over $50.
Gift cards cannot be exchanged for cash.
runs.see: Without --none, find must pick a line, so it prints the receipt rule.

runs.name: find-jsonl
runs.command: thinkthen find 'Which answer says how to reset a password?' --jsonl --field /text --input faq.jsonl
runs.see: Q1 holds the reset steps, and the whole record comes back.
